## Overview

The clustering panel clusters cancers from the cross-cancer similarity of their per-feature
age-effect profiles. The clustering is hierarchical (Ward.D2) with optimal
leaf ordering, applied to a distance matrix derived from per-layer Pearson
similarities averaged across molecular layers.

This script:

1. **Loads** per-cancer age-effect statistics for every layer the upstream
   pipeline produced (Methylation, RNA-seq, miRNA, RPPA, Mutation, SCNA).
2. **Filters** each layer to features with evidence of an age effect in at
   least one cancer.
3. **Diagnoses** each layer for two criteria that determine whether
   cross-cancer similarity can be computed reliably: post-filter feature count
   and pairwise feature overlap between cancers.
4. **Selects** layers for clustering. The diagnostic informs the decision;
   the included set itself is specified explicitly so the rationale for each
   layer's inclusion or exclusion is visible at the point of decision.
   Excluded layers are not discarded from the manuscript — they remain in
   the per-cancer counts; they are excluded only from the cross-cancer
   similarity step.
5. **Combines** retained layers via pairwise-available similarity averaging
   with a per-pair feature-overlap floor.
6. **Clusters** cancers from the resulting distance.

Each decision is explained inline next to the chunk that implements it.

```{r}
part1_imported_results <- readRDS(import_file)

layer_manifest       <- part1_imported_results$layer_manifest
result_file_manifest <- part1_imported_results$result_file_manifest
```

## Per-pair overlap floor

A meaningful Pearson correlation between two cancers needs them to share
enough features. We apply this as a *per-pair mask* during averaging — a
pair receives a layer's contribution only when that pair's overlap in that
layer meets the floor. This protects the combined similarity from noisy
contributions when a specific pair has very thin shared coverage in one
layer (relevant primarily for SCNA, where heme cancers have sparse copy-
number events).

```{r}
MIN_PAIR_OVERLAP <- 100
```

## Helper functions

### Optimal leaf ordering

`hcopt` performs Ward.D2 hierarchical clustering and reorders leaves to
minimize the sum of distances between adjacent tips. This does not change
which cancers cluster together; it only chooses the most readable left-to-
right arrangement among the equivalent orderings.

```{r}
hcopt <- function(d, HC = NULL, method = "ward.D2", members = NULL) {
  if (!requireNamespace("cba", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package 'cba' is required for optimal leaf ordering in the clustering.")
  }

  if (is.null(HC)) {
    HC <- stats::hclust(d, method = method, members = members)
  }

  ORD <- cba::order.optimal(d, merge = HC$merge)
  HC$merge <- ORD$merge
  HC$order <- ORD$order
  HC
}
```

### Pairwise feature overlap

For any feature × cancer matrix, the (i, j) entry of the overlap matrix is
the number of features for which both cancer i and cancer j have a non-NA
age-effect estimate. This is what `cor(..., use = "pairwise.complete.obs")`
silently uses; making it explicit lets us inspect and threshold on it.

```{r}
compute_pair_overlap <- function(mat) {
  present <- !is.na(mat)
  t(present) %*% present
}
```

### Per-layer matrix construction

For each layer we load the per-cancer regression results, extract the
single age-effect statistic the upstream pipeline reports (Wald t for
DESeq2, moderated t for limma, regression statistic for mutation/SCNA),
and assemble a feature × cancer matrix. Pearson is scale-invariant within a
layer, so the choice of statistic does not bias the layer's similarity.

We pre-filter to features reaching the layer's adjusted-p threshold in
**at least one cancer**. Rationale: features that are nowhere age-associated
do not carry tissue-of-origin information in age-effect space; they only add
noise to the cross-cancer Pearson. Methylation additionally has a top-
100,000 cap by significance recurrence — methylation has many more features
than the next-largest layer, and the cap is a practical compute control with
negligible impact on similarity (cap-removed features are nearly all
significant in only one cancer).

```{r}
process_layer_for_clustering <- function(layer_row, file_manifest) {
  files_tbl <- file_manifest %>%
    dplyr::filter(layer_id == layer_row$layer_id)

  if (layer_row$layer_id %in% c("RNAseq", "miRNA")) {
    files_tbl <- files_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(result_use == "unfiltered_deseq")
  } else if (layer_row$layer_id == "Mutation") {
    files_tbl <- files_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(result_use == "with_covariates_all")
  } else if (layer_row$layer_id == "SCNA") {
    files_tbl <- files_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(result_use == "with_covariates_gene_level")
  } else {
    files_tbl <- files_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(result_use == "limma")
  }

  if (nrow(files_tbl) == 0) {
    stop("No clustering input files were found for layer: ", layer_row$layer_id)
  }

  t_stats_list <- vector("list", nrow(files_tbl))
  pvals_list   <- vector("list", nrow(files_tbl))

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(files_tbl))) {
    project   <- files_tbl$Project[[i]]
    file_path <- files_tbl$file_path[[i]]

    x <- readRDS(file_path)

    # Per-layer feature extraction. Mutation results live under list element
    # "all"; SCNA splits amplifications and deletions into separate sublists,
    # so we encode them as AMP|gene and DEL|gene to keep direction
    # information distinct for clustering.
    if (layer_row$layer_id == "Mutation") {
      if (!"all" %in% names(x)) {
        stop("Mutation result file does not contain an 'all' entry: ", basename(file_path))
      }

      x <- x[["all"]] %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        dplyr::rename(Feature = gene_name)

    } else if (layer_row$layer_id == "SCNA") {
      if (!all(c("amplified_two_levels", "deleted_two_levels") %in% names(x))) {
        stop(
          "SCNA result file is missing amplified/deleted gene-level tables: ",
          basename(file_path)
        )
      }

      x <- dplyr::bind_rows(
        x[["amplified_two_levels"]] %>%
          as.data.frame() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(Feature = paste0("AMP|", feature_name)),
        x[["deleted_two_levels"]] %>%
          as.data.frame() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(Feature = paste0("DEL|", feature_name))
      )

    } else if (isTRUE(layer_row$feature_in_rownames)) {
      x <- x %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("Feature")

    } else {
      x <- x %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        dplyr::rename(Feature = dplyr::all_of(layer_row$feature_identifier))
    }

    required_cols <- c("Feature", layer_row$stat_col, layer_row$pval_col)
    missing_cols  <- setdiff(required_cols, colnames(x))

    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      stop(
        "Layer ", layer_row$layer_id,
        " is missing required columns in ", basename(file_path), ": ",
        paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")
      )
    }

    t_stats_list[[i]] <- x %>%
      dplyr::select(Feature, !!rlang::sym(layer_row$stat_col)) %>%
      dplyr::rename(!!project := !!rlang::sym(layer_row$stat_col))

    pvals_list[[i]] <- x %>%
      dplyr::select(Feature, !!rlang::sym(layer_row$pval_col)) %>%
      dplyr::rename(!!project := !!rlang::sym(layer_row$pval_col))
  }

  combined_t <- purrr::reduce(t_stats_list, dplyr::full_join, by = "Feature")
  combined_p <- purrr::reduce(pvals_list,   dplyr::full_join, by = "Feature")

  # Significance pre-filter: keep features reaching threshold in any cancer.
  significant_features <- combined_p %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_any(-Feature, ~ .x < layer_row$pval_threshold)) %>%
    dplyr::pull(Feature)

  filtered_t <- combined_t %>% dplyr::filter(Feature %in% significant_features)
  filtered_p <- combined_p %>% dplyr::filter(Feature %in% significant_features)

  # Optional per-layer cap (methylation only) to control compute.
  if (!is.na(layer_row$top_n)) {
    significance_counts <- filtered_p %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        Significant_Count = rowSums(
          dplyr::across(-Feature, ~ .x < layer_row$pval_threshold),
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      ) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Significant_Count))

    n_keep       <- min(layer_row$top_n, nrow(significance_counts))
    top_features <- significance_counts %>%
      dplyr::slice(seq_len(n_keep)) %>%
      dplyr::pull(Feature)

    filtered_t <- filtered_t %>% dplyr::filter(Feature %in% top_features)
  }

  filtered_t %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("Feature") %>%
    as.matrix()
}
```

## Load every available layer

We load all six layers the upstream pipeline produced. Two will turn out to
be unsuitable for cross-cancer similarity; we make that decision *after*
inspecting each layer's diagnostics, not before.

```{r}
all_layers <- layer_manifest$layer_id

all_layer_matrices <- purrr::map(
  split(layer_manifest, layer_manifest$layer_id)[all_layers],
  ~ process_layer_for_clustering(.x, result_file_manifest)
)
```

## Per-layer Pearson similarity and pair overlap

For each layer we compute (a) the cancer × cancer Pearson similarity using
all available pairs, and (b) the cancer × cancer matrix of how many features
each pair of cancers shares (i.e., have a non-NA age-effect estimate for in
both). The latter is what makes per-pair masking possible later.

```{r}
all_similarity_by_layer <- purrr::map(
  all_layer_matrices,
  ~ stats::cor(.x, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
)

all_pair_overlap_by_layer <- purrr::map(all_layer_matrices, compute_pair_overlap)
```

## Layer suitability diagnostics

We summarize each layer with:

- **Total features** (post-filter): how big is the feature universe?
- **Pairwise overlap** (min, median, max across cancer pairs): how much of
  that universe does an average pair actually share?

```{r}
summarize_pair_overlap <- function(overlap_mat) {
  vals <- as.numeric(overlap_mat[upper.tri(overlap_mat)])
  vals <- vals[is.finite(vals)]
  if (length(vals) == 0) {
    return(c(min = NA_real_, median = NA_real_, max = NA_real_))
  }
  c(min = min(vals), median = stats::median(vals), max = max(vals))
}

layer_diagnostics <- tibble::tibble(layer_id = all_layers) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_cancers      = purrr::map_int(layer_id, ~ ncol(all_layer_matrices[[.x]])),
    total_features = purrr::map_int(layer_id, ~ nrow(all_layer_matrices[[.x]])),
    overlap_stats  = purrr::map(layer_id, ~ summarize_pair_overlap(all_pair_overlap_by_layer[[.x]]))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    min_pair_overlap    = purrr::map_dbl(overlap_stats, "min"),
    median_pair_overlap = purrr::map_dbl(overlap_stats, "median"),
    max_pair_overlap    = purrr::map_dbl(overlap_stats, "max")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-overlap_stats)

layer_diagnostics
```

## Layer selection

The diagnostic above informs which layers are appropriate for cross-cancer
similarity. Two layers are excluded:

- **RPPA**: the panel is curated to a few hundred antibodies — too narrow a
  feature space to anchor cross-cancer similarity, and the dynamic range is
  much smaller than the genomics layers. This is a structural/measurement
  decision rather than a data-driven one. RPPA's per-cancer counts still
  appear in the count panel.

- **Mutation**: the per-cancer mutation regression applies a `min_group_size
  = 10` filter (a gene is tested only if both ≥ 10 mutated and ≥ 10 wild-
  type samples exist). This restricts each cancer's testable feature set to
  its recurrent driver genes, which are largely tissue-specific. The
  diagnostic above shows median pairwise feature overlap of ~1, far below
  what is needed for stable Pearson similarity. Mutation's per-cancer
  counts still appear in the count panel.

The remaining four layers — Methylation, RNA-seq, miRNA, SCNA — are
retained for clustering. SCNA passes the median-overlap criterion but has a
long left tail (e.g., heme cancers with sparse copy-number events); the
per-pair overlap floor will mask SCNA's contribution for those specific
pairs while leaving its contribution intact where it is well-supported.

```{r}
selected_layers <- c("Methylation", "RNAseq", "miRNA", "SCNA")
excluded_layers <- setdiff(all_layers, selected_layers)

stopifnot(all(selected_layers %in% all_layers))

# Restrict downstream objects to retained layers. The full set is preserved
# under the `all_*` names for diagnostic reproducibility.
layer_matrices        <- all_layer_matrices[selected_layers]
similarity_by_layer   <- all_similarity_by_layer[selected_layers]
pair_overlap_by_layer <- all_pair_overlap_by_layer[selected_layers]

# Cancers must appear in our most comprehensive layers (Methylation and
# RNA-seq) to enter the clustering. This serves as a quality floor on
# per-cancer similarity estimation; in practice every cancer in the cohort
# meets this requirement.
baseline_layers <- intersect(c("Methylation", "RNAseq"), selected_layers)
cancers_base    <- Reduce(
  intersect,
  purrr::map(similarity_by_layer[baseline_layers], colnames)
)
```

## Cross-layer similarity averaging with per-pair overlap floor

For each retained layer, we contribute its per-pair similarity to the
average — but only where the pair shares at least `MIN_PAIR_OVERLAP`
features in that layer. The denominator (`S_n`) tracks how many layers
actually contributed to each pair, so pairs with a layer masked out are
averaged from the remaining layers, not penalized.

```{r}
S_sum <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = length(cancers_base),
  ncol = length(cancers_base),
  dimnames = list(cancers_base, cancers_base)
)
S_n <- S_sum

for (nm in selected_layers) {
  S <- similarity_by_layer[[nm]]
  O <- pair_overlap_by_layer[[nm]]

  common <- intersect(cancers_base, colnames(S))
  if (length(common) < 2) next

  S_sub <- S[common, common, drop = FALSE]
  O_sub <- O[common, common, drop = FALSE]

  valid <- is.finite(S_sub) & O_sub >= MIN_PAIR_OVERLAP

  S_sum[common, common] <- S_sum[common, common] + ifelse(valid, S_sub, 0)
  S_n[common, common]   <- S_n[common, common] + ifelse(valid, 1, 0)
}

if (any(S_n == 0)) {
  zero_pairs <- which(S_n == 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  stop(
    "Some cancer pairs received no layer contributions after applying the ",
    "per-pair overlap floor. First affected pair: ",
    rownames(S_n)[zero_pairs[1, 1]], " / ", colnames(S_n)[zero_pairs[1, 2]]
  )
}

average_similarity <- S_sum / S_n
diag(average_similarity) <- 1

average_distance <- as.dist(1 - average_similarity)
```

## Hierarchical clustering with optimal leaf ordering

```{r}
hc_pw_opt    <- hcopt(average_distance, method = "ward.D2")
cancer_order <- hc_pw_opt$labels[hc_pw_opt$order]
```

## Save clustering results

The saved object preserves every field the figure script reads
(`selected_layers`, `layer_matrices`, `similarity_by_layer`,
`pair_overlap_by_layer`, `average_similarity`, `hclust`, `thresholds`) and
adds the diagnostic context (`layer_diagnostics`, `excluded_layers`,
`all_*` siblings) so the inclusion decisions are reproducible from this
file alone.

```{r}
pancancer_clustering_results <- list(
  # Decisions and parameters
  selected_layers   = selected_layers,
  excluded_layers   = excluded_layers,
  baseline_layers   = baseline_layers,
  layer_diagnostics = layer_diagnostics,
  thresholds        = list(
    MIN_PAIR_OVERLAP = MIN_PAIR_OVERLAP
  ),

  # Per-layer data — retained layers (used downstream)
  layer_ids             = selected_layers,
  layer_matrices        = layer_matrices,
  similarity_by_layer   = similarity_by_layer,
  pair_overlap_by_layer = pair_overlap_by_layer,

  # Per-layer data — full set (kept for transparency / diagnostics)
  all_layer_matrices        = all_layer_matrices,
  all_similarity_by_layer   = all_similarity_by_layer,
  all_pair_overlap_by_layer = all_pair_overlap_by_layer,

  # Combined similarity and clustering
  average_similarity = average_similarity,
  n_layers_per_pair  = S_n,
  average_distance   = average_distance,
  hclust             = hc_pw_opt,
  cancer_order       = cancer_order
)

saveRDS(
  pancancer_clustering_results,
  file.path(out_dir, "pancancer_clustering_results.rds")
)

utils::write.csv(
  layer_diagnostics,
  file = file.path(tables_dir, "fig1b_layer_diagnostics.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

utils::write.csv(
  data.frame(Project = cancer_order),
  file = file.path(tables_dir, "fig1b_cancer_order.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
